payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and extend storage-system longevity. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit corrected the prototype’s accelerated cycling result to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold. The battery has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg and a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must be suspended. The chemistry separates power capacity, determined by stack size, from energy capacity, determined by tank size.
